system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: model serving APIs
G2: Kubernetes
G3: MLflow
G4: Airflow/Kubeflow
G5: deep learning beyond a course
G6: GCP infrastructure
G7: CI/CD for ML

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming he deployed models as APIs or built ML pipelines on Kubernetes/Kubeflow
T2: Listing MLflow, Airflow, Kubernetes, SageMaker because MLE ads require them
T3: Presenting the PyTorch course project as professional deep learning
T4: Claiming he deployed the Streamlit app to Cloud Run (platform team did)
T5: Retitling him as ML Engineer in the experience section
T6: Old cover letter is to his current employer and describes him as junior analyst

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist | Applied Machine Learning
Email: tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | Phone: +44 7700 900110 | LinkedIn:
linkedin.com/in/tmh-example
PROFILE
Data scientist with 6 years of experience in analytics and data science. Strong foundation in statistics
and Python, with experience developing forecasting and churn propensity models. Builds analyses
and models that inform operational and customer decisions, and communicates results clearly to
business stakeholders. Interested in moving towards machine learning engineering.
EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox (meal-kit subscriptions) Feb 2022–Present
• Built a weekly per-recipe demand forecasting model using LightGBM and calendar features. The
model is used by operations to order ingredients; WAPE decreased from 23% to 14%, and food
waste fell by an estimated 9%.
• Developed a churn propensity model using XGBoost to target retention offers, with uplift validated
using a holdout.
• Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for growth and product teams; built the
team’s sequential testing calculator.
• Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
• Present results to leadership monthly.
Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | Glasgow Sep 2020–Jan 2022
• Conducted customer segmentation and tariff analysis using R and SQL.
• Automated monthly regulator reports using R Markdown.
EDUCATION
MSc Statistics | University of the Lothians | 2020 | Distinction
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand
BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019
SKILLS
Programming and data: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels), R
(tidyverse, brms), SQL (BigQuery)
Data and engineering tools: dbt, Git, Jupyter, Looker
Machine learning and analytics: Demand forecasting, churn propensity modelling, A/B testing,
causal inference, time-series forecasting, Bayesian statistics
LANGUAGES
English (native) | Swahili (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Team,
I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone
Payments. I bring six years of experience in analytics and data science, with a strong
foundation in Python and statistics and hands-on experience building models that inform
operational and customer decisions. I am now looking to apply my data-science and production
analytics experience in a machine learning engineering environment, and the opportunity to
help make support faster and more useful for merchants particularly interests me.
At Thistlebox, I built a weekly per-recipe demand forecasting model using LightGBM and
calendar features. Operations uses it to order ingredients; forecast error (WAPE) fell from 23%
to 14%, and food waste decreased by an estimated 9%. I also developed an XGBoost churn
propensity model to target retention offers, with uplift validated using a holdout. I also design
and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests each year for growth and product teams and built the
team’s sequential testing calculator. Alongside this work, I write production SQL in BigQuery
(GCP), maintain dbt models for the analytics layer, and use Git. These experiences have taught
me to connect modeling choices to practical outcomes and to communicate results clearly to
stakeholders.
Quillstone’s work on AI systems that answer merchant questions and support agents appeals to
me because it brings applied machine learning close to real customer needs. I would bring
experience taking forecasting, customer-propensity, and experimentation work from business
questions to decision-useful outputs, while collaborating with product and operational teams. I
am keen to build on that foundation in a team that takes ownership, shares context openly, and
learns from mistakes.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience could contribute to Quillstone’s Customer Operations AI team.
Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
